w: One of the two glacial Lakes of Covadonga, sitting at 1,108m in the Picos de Europa. It covers about 8 hectares but is barely 2 metres deep and eutrophic, ringed by karst peaks near the Covadonga Sanctuary. Its twin, Lake Enol, lies a short walk away across the plateau.
s: Shallow glacial lake beside its twin, Enol
_facts: Altitude 1,108m
Max depth just over 2m
Covers about 8 hectares
One of two Lakes of Covadonga

w: The larger of the twin glacial Lakes of Covadonga, reached by a curving road from Arriondas. Every 8 September a submerged image of the Virgin Mary is raised from the water and paraded in procession; on 25 July shepherds gather for the Fiesta del Pastor. The founding site of Picos de Europa National Park, 1918.
s: Where a submerged Virgin Mary is raised each September
_facts: 1,070m above sea level
Founding site of Picos de Europa NP (1918)
Annual Fiesta del Pastor, 25 July

w: Built entirely of pink limestone in Neo-Romanesque style, designed by German architect Roberto Frassinelli and completed by Federico Aparici y Soriano between 1877 and 1901. Rome granted it basilica status that same year, cementing Covadonga's place as one of Spanish Catholicism's most storied sites.
_facts: Made entirely of pink limestone
Designated a basilica in 1901

n: Monasterio de Santo Toribio de Liébana
w: Founded before the 6th century near Potes, one of only five Catholic sites -- with Rome, Jerusalem, Santiago de Compostela and Caravaca de la Cruz -- permitted to grant perpetual indulgences. It holds what is claimed to be the largest surviving fragment of the True Cross, kept in a gilded silver reliquary.
s: Guards the largest known fragment of the True Cross
_facts: Founded before the 6th century
One of five sites worldwide with perpetual indulgence rights
Holds a Lignum Crucis relic of the True Cross

w: A small church near Covadonga holding outsized history: Pelagius of Asturias, who defeated a Moorish army at Covadonga in 718 to launch the Reconquista, was originally buried here with his wife. The battle he won is traditionally marked as the start of nearly eight centuries of Christian reconquest of Iberia.
s: Original burial place of the Reconquista's founder
_facts: Original burial site of Pelagius of Asturias
Pelagius won the Battle of Covadonga in 718
Considered the start of the Reconquista

w: The oldest standing building in the Sanctuary of Covadonga, set beside the Holy Cave that anchors the site. Declared Bien de Interes Cultural in 1884, this collegiate church predates the basilica by decades and remains the historic core around which Covadonga's pilgrimage complex grew.
s: The Sanctuary of Covadonga's oldest building
_facts: Declared Bien de Interes Cultural in 1884
Oldest building in the Sanctuary of Covadonga
Stands next to the Holy Cave

w: A 1,610m mountain pass on the N-621 linking Leon with Cantabria, just 800m from the southern edge of Picos de Europa National Park. Endangered Cantabrian brown bears use the pass as a wildlife corridor between valleys protected under the EU's Natura 2000 network.
s: A mountain pass used as a brown bear corridor
_facts: Elevation 1,610m
800m from the Picos de Europa NP border
Wildlife corridor for endangered Cantabrian brown bears
